usedHookFrames: Influence-ch01: A fax machine blinks, a title lands, and a whole decision starts moving before the facts do.
Influence-ch02: A plastic spoon of jam can feel heavier than a price tag when it arrives first.
Influence-ch03: A compliment in a cafeteria aisle can make a weak answer feel warmer than it is.
Influence-ch04: A quiet pool deck can make danger look ordinary for the ten seconds that matter.
Influence-ch05: A white coat can make a wrong dose look quieter than the label in your hand.
Influence-ch06: The last two in stock can make a bad stroller feel like a closing door.
Influence-ch07: A name in marker on a pledge board can pull harder than a trainer shouting.
Influence-ch08: The word family can warm a break room, or make a bad trade harder to refuse.
Influence-ch09: When six alarms ring at once, the loudest cue can pretend to be judgment.
usedCounterFrames: Influence-ch01: Fast cues are not foolish. They help people move through crowded days. The danger starts when a cue that usually helps begins to stand in for the choice itself.
Influence-ch02: Reciprocity is not a flaw. It keeps social life decent. The trap is letting any first gift write the size, timing, and target of the return.
Influence-ch03: Liking is not proof of bad judgment. It is useful social data. Trouble starts when warmth, similarity, praise, or shared colors gets treated as proof of competence or truth.
Influence-ch04: Other people are often useful evidence. The trap appears when everyone is using everyone else as evidence and nobody is checking the thing itself.
Influence-ch05: Authority is useful because real expertise saves time and lives. The risk is not respect. The risk is letting titles, uniforms, status, or fame answer questions outside their proof.
Influence-ch06: Scarcity can signal real value, but it also changes desire by threatening loss. The feeling of urgency is not the same as evidence of fit.
Influence-ch07: Consistency is useful because it lets people keep promises and build identity. It becomes costly when old statements keep ruling after the facts have changed.

Influence-ch08: Unity is deeper than liking. It comes from shared identity, kinship, place, struggle, or belonging. That depth can call people to real care, or make unfair asks feel disloyal to question.
Influence-ch09: The modern problem is not that people are less thoughtful. It is that speed, noise, and choice make shortcuts more necessary, which makes clean cues and abusive cues more powerful.
usedTryThisNowFrames: Influence-ch01: Pick one yes you gave today. Write the cue that moved you first, then write one fact you would have checked if the cue had not arrived.
Influence-ch02: Think of one favor or gift you received this week. Say aloud what you actually owe, if anything, and what the giver may be hoping you feel you owe.
Influence-ch03: Before your next yes to someone you like, write one sentence naming the warmth and one sentence naming the evidence that stands apart from it.
Influence-ch04: At your next group pause, ask one direct question or take one small visible step instead of reading silence as certainty.
Influence-ch05: Before following an expert cue today, name the exact field of expertise and one fact you still need to check for this case.
Influence-ch06: When something feels urgent because it may disappear, write what you wanted before the scarcity cue and what new fact, if any, the cue adds.
Influence-ch07: Find one promise you are keeping mainly because you said it out loud. Write the original reason and whether that reason is still true today.
Influence-ch08: When someone says we today, write who is included, what is being asked, and whether the shared identity truly owns that cost.
Influence-ch09: Before one fast choice today, say the cue out loud: authority, scarcity, liking, proof, unity, or reciprocity. Then choose with the cue named.
